How do I get from Phuket to Koh Samui? | Fly with Bangkok Airways (about 6–8 flights a day, about 1 hour), or take a joint bus-and-ferry or van-and-ferry ticket via Donsak pier, which takes about 6.5–10 hours.
How long is the flight from Phuket to Samui? | About 1 hour gate to gate on Bangkok Airways, the only airline flying the route nonstop.
Is there a ferry from Phuket to Koh Samui? | No, Phuket and Samui are on opposite coasts of the peninsula, so boats only cover the last leg from Donsak pier near Surat Thani after a 4–6 hour road journey.
How do I get from Krabi to Koh Samui? | Fly with Bangkok Airways (1–2 flights a day, about 45–50 minutes) or take a van-and-ferry ticket from Krabi Town or Ao Nang via Donsak, about 5–6.5 hours for roughly 400–850 THB.
Can I stop at Khao Sok between Krabi and Samui? | Yes, Khao Sok National Park lies on Route 401 between the Andaman coast and Surat Thani; plan at least 2 days and 1 night rather than a day trip, because it is 4–6 hours from Samui.
When is the best time to combine Phuket and Samui? | January to April, when both coasts are usually dry; from May to September Samui is drier than the Andaman side, and in November the Andaman side is better.
Is it cheaper to go by bus and ferry? | Yes, overland tickets cost about 450–1,500 THB compared with about 3,700 THB or more for a flight, but they take a full day instead of about an hour.
